brief.background: A small operations team must route maintenance requests.
brief.painPoint: Shared inboxes lose context and repeat the same handoffs.
brief.valueHypothesis: Make routing reasons and missing information visible. Value is unmeasured.
brief.technicalCombination: Start with a checklist, rules and owner lookup. Add no model by default.
brief.scaleTrigger: Test retrieval or a bounded LLM only if free-text ambiguity dominates.
brief.weaknessCounterargument: The sample is synthetic. A new tool may cost more effort than the inbox.
brief.nextCheck: Observe 20 anonymized requests against the current workflow before building.

problem: Route maintenance requests with clear ownership without automating safety decisions.
currentWorkflow: A shared inbox and spreadsheet are the assumed baseline; no real team has been observed.
decisionToSupport: Suggest the responsible team and missing fields for human review.
nonGoals: No automatic shutdown, repair approval, purchasing or external messages.

sources.supports: An illustrative inbox with structured request types and ambiguous descriptions.
sources.limits: No customer observations, real policies or measured business outcomes.

requirements.need: Every suggestion needs an owner or an explicit handoff.
requirements.acceptance: Unknown owners are deferred rather than invented.

requirements.need: Suggestions must not execute maintenance actions.
requirements.acceptance: Safety and approval questions go to the maintenance lead.

alternatives.mechanism: A coordinator reads requests and chooses an owner.
alternatives.dataNeeded: Current procedure and a maintained ownership list.
alternatives.worksWhen: Low volume and familiar request categories.
alternatives.failsWhen: Repeated handoffs become frequent or ownership is unclear.
alternatives.costAndOperations: No new service; requires coordinator attention.
alternatives.reason: Retain as the observed baseline before adding software.

alternatives.mechanism: Map structured request types to reviewed ownership rules.
alternatives.dataNeeded: Stable categories and a versioned owner mapping.
alternatives.worksWhen: Requests contain the necessary structured fields.
alternatives.failsWhen: Free-text ambiguity dominates or mappings drift.
alternatives.costAndOperations: Small local script or existing portal; maintain rules.
alternatives.reason: Provides explicit reasons without assuming an LLM is necessary.

alternatives.mechanism: Retrieve reviewed procedures and draft a routing suggestion.
alternatives.dataNeeded: Representative requests, source policies and deferral labels.
alternatives.worksWhen: Observed ambiguity repeatedly defeats the simpler baseline.
alternatives.failsWhen: Source evidence is missing or model output is treated as authority.
alternatives.costAndOperations: Adds provider cost, latency and evaluation ownership.
alternatives.reason: Evaluate only after showing a real gap in checklist and rules.

assumptions.statement: Most requests may be simple enough for a checklist.
assumptions.impact: If requests are mostly free text, fixed rules may miss important context.
assumptions.verification: Review anonymized requests with the current coordinator.

scenarios.trigger: A request contains a new asset with no owner mapping.
scenarios.expectedResponse: Ask for the owner and retain the original request.
scenarios.requiredDesignChange: Separate unknown ownership from a negative eligibility decision.
scenarios.evaluationMethod: Design desk review only; no product execution is claimed.

scenarios.trigger: An incoming description asks the system to shut equipment down.
scenarios.expectedResponse: Provide a human handoff; do not issue control commands.
scenarios.requiredDesignChange: Treat request text as data, not permission to execute actions.
scenarios.evaluationMethod: Design desk review of the permission and handoff boundary.

claims.statement: Clear routing evidence may reduce repeated handoffs.
claims.limit: No real task completion, time saving or user preference has been measured.

deployment.runtime: A local file or existing portal is sufficient for the first study.
deployment.identityBoundary: Only authenticated coordinators can propose routing changes.
deployment.dataBoundary: Use anonymized requests; keep asset and customer details local.
deployment.capacityModel: Measure request volume and operator wait before selecting a service runtime.
deployment.failureRecovery: Retain original text and the last human owner on failures.
deployment.releaseRollback: Version routing rules and restore the previous reviewed version.
deployment.observability: Count deferrals and correction reasons without logging private text.
deployment.operatingOwner: The maintenance lead owns policy changes and exception handling.

nextValidation: Compare checklist and rules on the same 20 anonymized requests with the coordinator.

critiques.challenge: The inbox may already be sufficient for a small team.
critiques.response: Keep the existing inbox as the baseline.
critiques.residualRisk: A new workflow could add work instead of removing it.

critiques.challenge: Asset ownership may be incomplete or out of date.
critiques.response: Mark unknown owners and ask the policy owner to verify.
critiques.residualRisk: Routing quality remains unmeasured without real requests.

critiques.challenge: A request could ask for a high-impact equipment action.
critiques.response: Keep all control actions outside the assistant scope.
critiques.residualRisk: Human procedures and actual system permissions still need review.
